1	# Cycle checklists
2	
3	Checklists for the moments where slips happen: committing, pushing, closing out. The full
4	protocol, with rationale and recovery procedures, is
5	[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md). On any disagreement, that file wins. Re-read
6	the relevant checklist immediately before the action. Don't run it from memory.
7	
8	Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and
9	converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
10	Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).
11	
12	## The cycle at a glance
13	
14	Every change runs as a **cycle** with three phases: Preparation -> Work -> Close-out. The
15	phases always happen, but there are two styles. A **multi-step** cycle commits them
16	individually, as a ladder of steps (the Preparation commit is optional); a
17	**single-step** cycle folds all three into one commit when the change is straightforward, so
18	that one commit is the close-out and carries its duties, mandatory validation included. So a
19	single-step cycle is one commit, and a multi-step is minimum two (a Work commit plus the
20	close-out), typically three or more (the definition is
21	[AGENTS.md's Terminology](../AGENTS.md#terminology)). The
22	ladder lists a cycle's steps in order and identifies each by its title, with no number and no
23	version. Where the version-of-record lives and how often it is bumped are in
24	[versioning.md](versioning.md). Read [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md) before any commit
25	work, and before any push, cycle or not.
26	
27	## Cycles run on a bookmark
28	
29	A cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work repo, created at the opening and named by the
30	cycle title's slug (the anchor algorithm in
31	[Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). `main` advances only when the
32	finished cycle lands on it; nothing pushes straight to `main`. The bot repo needs no bookmark:
33	its `main` rides the tip of its linear narrative.
34	
35	- **The bookmark is the unit of review.** Everything the cycle does is visible as one line
36	  against `main`, and until it lands the whole line is a draft that can be reshaped
37	  ([Topic bookmarks are drafts](#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts)). Landing is the single approval
38	  that makes the cycle permanent.
39	- **Create at the opening**, land at the close-out. Commands are in
40	  [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), and the opening's other duties are in
41	  the [Opening checklist](#opening-checklist) below.
42	- **A single-step cycle still gets one.** The saving is not worth the exception, and a
43	  one-commit line is exactly the case where a pre-landing rewrite is cheapest.
44	- **The permanent branch is whatever this project calls it** (`main` here). A long-lived program
45	  bookmark is a different animal, governed by
46	  [Long-lived bookmarks](jj.md#long-lived-bookmarks-merge-only-by-default-deletable-once-merged).
47	
48	**Why:** a cycle that pushes `main` directly makes every correction a coordinated force-push of
49	published history. Landing costs one command and buys free rewrites for the whole cycle.
50	
51	## Opening checklist
52	
53	At the cycle's opening, before the first Work commit:
54	
55	1. Create the cycle's bookmark ([Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
56	2. Move the picked-up item into `TODO.md > ## In Progress` and write the **six provisional
57	   items** there, all six required. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress`'s
58	   own level, and the other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###`
59	   title, `####` items; under a program heading, each one deeper):
60	   - **title**, which becomes the chores section header at close-out
61	   - **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
62	   - **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad
63	   - **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?"
64	   - **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [[N]] [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with
65	     `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (the closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`,
66	     unlinked until its gotchas subsection exists)
67	   - **deliberation**: how the five above were decided (`_None._` when there was nothing to
68	     deliberate)
69	   A `Ladder details` area follows the six: one subsection per rung, headed by the rung's
70	   exact title, opened at laddering with the rung's intent and completed as rungs land; the
71	   closing rung's is created at close-out only if gotchas occurred (see the protocol's
72	   [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation)).
73	3. Sweep `## Done` per [Retiring Done entries](notes.md#retiring-done-entries), then bump the
74	   version-of-record.
75	
76	Nothing is opened in the chores file here. The block is the cycle's only home until close-out
77	moves it. See [Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).
78	
79	**Why the acceptance check:** a cycle's own checklists are per-commit instruments and every one
80	of them can pass while the banner claim is false. Measured in a seven-cycle program opened
81	against "end subprocess spawning": its close-out claimed the goal met, with about twenty spawn
82	sites surviving, two inside the facade the program built. A measurement or performance claim is
83	the shape most exposed, since "we measured it" is easy to believe and hard to notice you have not
84	done. Being provisional, the check can also be revised *toward* what was achieved, which is the
85	same failure by a slower route. A changed check is one of the things the deliberation justifies.
86	
87	## Committing vs pushing
88	
89	A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`. Never pre-commit it with `jj commit`. Push's
90	commit stages commit both repos with the approved title/body and stamp each new commit's
91	`ochid:` trailer (see [ochid trailers](jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)). A
92	pre-committed rung leaves `@` empty and push mints a stamped empty duplicate. In
93	an instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
94	is asked for by name ("local commit", "just `jj commit`") and is only for work that never
95	publishes (local-only saves and loop-and-squash intermediates), with no `ochid:`. The approval
96	around a push, interactive by default and waived only by an explicit scoped delegation, is the
97	cycle protocol's [Pushing policy](cycle-protocol.md#policy).
98	
99	## Topic bookmarks are drafts
100	
101	A topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on a permanent branch. Pushed there is not published.
102	So keep the series inside it self-consistent: inserting or reordering a step edits the ladder in
103	the rungs that already committed an older version of it, not only at the tip.
104	
105	- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
106	  `jj describe`, so hard rule 4 stays intact and the `ochid:` trailers ride along untouched
107	  (they carry change ids, which survive a rewrite).
108	- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
109	- **Exceptions, where self-consistency is not worth its cost**: the bookmark has already landed;
110	  another branch is stacked on it, so the rewrite becomes someone else's rebase; or the ladder
111	  is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.
112	
113	The squash-form ladder below never meets this, since nothing on it is pushed. The rule is for the
114	multi-commit shape, whose rungs publish one at a time. Full statement in the protocol's
115	[Topic bookmarks are drafts](cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).
116	
117	## Per-commit checklist
118	
119	Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out), per the protocol's
120	[Per-commit flow](cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow):
121	
122	1. Mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
123	2. Do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop and surface it.
124	3. Flip `(current)` -> `(done)`, before validation and the commit, and complete the rung's
125	   `Ladder details` subsection with the conceptual delta (its intent stub was opened when the
126	   rung was laddered; the ladder itself stays a bare ToC). See the protocol's
127	   [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation).
128	4. Bump the version-of-record to this commit's version (the suffix scheme is in
129	   [versioning.md](versioning.md)). The opening checklist's bump already covers a Preparation
130	   commit.
131	5. Validate the artifact (the medium-specific commands are in [custom.md](../custom.md)).
132	   Skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out.
133	6. Stop and ask the user, "please review", as this is the bottom of the review loop. Do not present
134	   a description as we iterate until the user reviews and says "continue|go|.." indicating the work
135	   review is likely complete.
136	7. Once the work review is complete, write the description: a conventional title, then a body in
137	   prose.md's [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form) (an intro paragraph stating the
138	   general problem, `*` bullets for its facets, `-` bullets for solutions, a `-` solving the
139	   nearest enclosing problem), sized per [Line widths](prose.md#line-widths). No version in
140	   either, no file list (the diff is the mechanical record), and no deliberation (chores, todo,
141	   and the session hold that). See [Commit description](cycle-protocol.md#commit-description).
142	8. Show title + body and stop for review. This review covers the push only when the user's go
143	   explicitly includes it.
144	9. On the user's go: `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."`. Never pre-commit with
145	   `jj commit`; never hand-write `ochid:` trailers.
146	
147	## Ladder (sub-cycle) checklist
148	
149	Within a sub-cycle ladder, per the protocol's
150	[per-Work-commit contract](cycle-protocol.md#per-work-commit-contract-within-a-ladder):
151	
152	1. `jj new -R .`: fresh empty `@`.
153	2. Do the commit's work.
154	3. Run the fast validation (named in [custom.md](../custom.md)). Non-negotiable.
155	4. `jj describe -m "..." -m "..." -R .`: scratch working title. This first-time authoring is
156	   the one permitted describe. The commit is never published and never carries a trailer.
157	
158	Nothing on a ladder is pushed. The close-out squash
159	(`jj squash --from "<base>..@-" --into @ -u -R .`) collapses it, and `vc-x1 push` then
160	publishes the single commit.
161	
162	## Before any push
163	
164	- This specific push has the user's explicit approval. Approval of a plan that includes a push
165	  is not push approval. "Commit and push" names the destination, not a waiver of the reviews.
166	  Only an explicit scoped delegation ("do all of X, don't check in") waives the stops, for that
167	  bounded task only. Delegation waives stops, never flow (records, validation, the bookmark
168	  discipline; see the protocol's [Policy](cycle-protocol.md#policy)), and destructive ops
169	  still pause.
170	- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
171	- Closing words are already written. Nothing follows the turn's final push (next checklist).
172	
173	## After the final push: hard stop
174	
175	Once the turn's final push or bot-repo squash-push is invoked, do no further work: no
176	verification, no summary, no next-step offers, no edits, until the user speaks. Put all closing
177	words *before* the invoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a visible token
178	after the tool returns. If so, emit a bare acknowledgment only (e.g. "landed"), never a summary
179	or more work. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's direction. A standing
180	delegation makes intermediate pushes just steps; the hard stop lands on the turn's *final*
181	push. See
182	[After push or squash-push](cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-squash-push-stop-and-wait).
183	
184	## Close-out checklist
185	
186	The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
187	[Close-out](cycle-protocol.md#close-out):
188	
189	1. **Run the acceptance check** the opening stated, and record what it showed in the
190	   `## In Progress` block, whether or not it passed. A check that was never run is a failed
191	   close-out, and a check that failed is a finding, not a reason to quietly restate the banner.
192	2. **Finalize the six items in place**: sync the title if the scope shifted, replace the
193	   provisional solution statement with what was done, drop the ladder's `(current)` / `(done)`
194	   markers, add any design subsections, and write the closing rung's gotchas subsection
195	   (problem/solution form) if closing surfaced any.
196	3. **Move the block** into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, which is what creates the section.
197	   Four transforms, two of which fail silently: headings one level deeper, rung refs renumbered
198	   into the destination's namespace, repo-root-relative links gain `../`, forward-looking notes
199	   rewritten. See [Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections). Add the title-only
200	   `## Table of Contents` entry.
201	4. Write the `## Done` entry: the version, then a bold title line with its chores `[N]` ref,
202	   detail as sub-bullets (see [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form)). Replace the
203	   `## In Progress` block with `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
204	5. Full validation, mandatory.
205	6. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
206	7. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
207	   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
208	   [in the protocol](cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe). Its step 4 is
209	   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
210	8. **Land the bookmark** on the user's go. Until this, nothing the cycle pushed is permanent.
211	   Once `main` contains the bookmark, delete it, locally and remotely. See
212	   [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land).
213	9. Backfill the chores as-built ladder refs (and any remaining legacy `Commits:` lines) for the
214	   commits landing just made permanent, which is the whole cycle rather than the previous push's
215	   share. Never record a SHA that is not on a permanent branch. The backfill edits ride the next
216	   push (a commit cannot record its own SHA).
217	
218	## vc-x1 push behaviors to keep in mind
219	
220	Three, independent of project language:
221	
222	- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 assumes nothing about a repo's contents beyond
223	  `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`, and runs no build or tests. The medium's validation is the
224	  per-commit flow's job, run *before* invoking `vc-x1 push`. The one check that remains is
225	  `push-work` verifying the bookmark's remote refs are tracked, which is its own precondition.
226	- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume. Every stage no-ops when its
227	  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If a run fails, push stops and
228	  reports. Getting the repos back to a sensible state is the user's call, not something the
229	  tool infers.
230	- **ochid trailers** are injected by `vc-x1 push` itself, so don't hand-write them into the
231	  commit body or `--title`/`--body`.

finished cycle lands on it; nothing pushes straight to `main`. The bot repo needs no bookmark:
its `main` rides the tip of its linear narrative.

- **The bookmark is the unit of review.** Everything the cycle does is visible as one line
  against `main`, and until it lands the whole line is a draft that can be reshaped
  ([Topic bookmarks are drafts](#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts)). Landing is the single approval
  that makes the cycle permanent.
- **Create at the opening**, land at the close-out. Commands are in
  [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), and the opening's other duties are in
  the [Opening checklist](#opening-checklist) below.
- **A single-step cycle still gets one.** The saving is not worth the exception, and a
  one-commit line is exactly the case where a pre-landing rewrite is cheapest.
- **The permanent branch is whatever this project calls it** (`main` here). A long-lived program
  bookmark is a different animal, governed by
  [Long-lived bookmarks](jj.md#long-lived-bookmarks-merge-only-by-default-deletable-once-merged).

**Why:** a cycle that pushes `main` directly makes every correction a coordinated force-push of
published history. Landing costs one command and buys free rewrites for the whole cycle.

## Opening checklist

At the cycle's opening, before the first Work commit:

1. Create the cycle's bookmark ([Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
2. Move the picked-up item into `TODO.md > ## In Progress` and write the **six provisional
   items** there, all six required. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress`'s
   own level, and the other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###`
   title, `####` items; under a program heading, each one deeper):
   - **title**, which becomes the chores section header at close-out
   - **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
   - **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad
   - **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?"
   - **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [[N]] [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with
     `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (the closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`,
     unlinked until its gotchas subsection exists)
   - **deliberation**: how the five above were decided (`_None._` when there was nothing to
     deliberate)
   A `Ladder details` area follows the six: one subsection per rung, headed by the rung's
   exact title, opened at laddering with the rung's intent and completed as rungs land; the
   closing rung's is created at close-out only if gotchas occurred (see the protocol's
   [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation)).
3. Sweep `## Done` per [Retiring Done entries](notes.md#retiring-done-entries), then bump the
   version-of-record.

Nothing is opened in the chores file here. The block is the cycle's only home until close-out
moves it. See [Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

**Why the acceptance check:** a cycle's own checklists are per-commit instruments and every one
of them can pass while the banner claim is false. Measured in a seven-cycle program opened
against "end subprocess spawning": its close-out claimed the goal met, with about twenty spawn
sites surviving, two inside the facade the program built. A measurement or performance claim is
the shape most exposed, since "we measured it" is easy to believe and hard to notice you have not
done. Being provisional, the check can also be revised *toward* what was achieved, which is the
same failure by a slower route. A changed check is one of the things the deliberation justifies.

## Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`. Never pre-commit it with `jj commit`. Push's
commit stages commit both repos with the approved title/body and stamp each new commit's
`ochid:` trailer (see [ochid trailers](jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)). A
pre-committed rung leaves `@` empty and push mints a stamped empty duplicate. In
an instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
is asked for by name ("local commit", "just `jj commit`") and is only for work that never
publishes (local-only saves and loop-and-squash intermediates), with no `ochid:`. The approval
around a push, interactive by default and waived only by an explicit scoped delegation, is the
cycle protocol's [Pushing policy](cycle-protocol.md#policy).

## Topic bookmarks are drafts

A topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on a permanent branch. Pushed there is not published.
So keep the series inside it self-consistent: inserting or reordering a step edits the ladder in
the rungs that already committed an older version of it, not only at the tip.

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so hard rule 4 stays intact and the `ochid:` trailers ride along untouched
  (they carry change ids, which survive a rewrite).
- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
- **Exceptions, where self-consistency is not worth its cost**: the bookmark has already landed;
  another branch is stacked on it, so the rewrite becomes someone else's rebase; or the ladder
  is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

The squash-form ladder below never meets this, since nothing on it is pushed. The rule is for the
multi-commit shape, whose rungs publish one at a time. Full statement in the protocol's
[Topic bookmarks are drafts](cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).

## Per-commit checklist

Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out), per the protocol's
[Per-commit flow](cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow):

1. Mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
2. Do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop and surface it.
3. Flip `(current)` -> `(done)`, before validation and the commit, and complete the rung's
   `Ladder details` subsection with the conceptual delta (its intent stub was opened when the
   rung was laddered; the ladder itself stays a bare ToC). See the protocol's
   [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation).
4. Bump the version-of-record to this commit's version (the suffix scheme is in
   [versioning.md](versioning.md)). The opening checklist's bump already covers a Preparation
   commit.
5. Validate the artifact (the medium-specific commands are in [custom.md](../custom.md)).
   Skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out.
6. Stop and ask the user, "please review", as this is the bottom of the review loop. Do not present
   a description as we iterate until the user reviews and says "continue|go|.." indicating the work
   review is likely complete.
7. Once the work review is complete, write the description: a conventional title, then a body in
   prose.md's [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form) (an intro paragraph stating the
   general problem, `*` bullets for its facets, `-` bullets for solutions, a `-` solving the
   nearest enclosing problem), sized per [Line widths](prose.md#line-widths). No version in
   either, no file list (the diff is the mechanical record), and no deliberation (chores, todo,
   and the session hold that). See [Commit description](cycle-protocol.md#commit-description).
8. Show title + body and stop for review. This review covers the push only when the user's go
   explicitly includes it.
9. On the user's go: `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."`. Never pre-commit with
   `jj commit`; never hand-write `ochid:` trailers.

## Ladder (sub-cycle) checklist

Within a sub-cycle ladder, per the protocol's
[per-Work-commit contract](cycle-protocol.md#per-work-commit-contract-within-a-ladder):

1. `jj new -R .`: fresh empty `@`.
2. Do the commit's work.
3. Run the fast validation (named in [custom.md](../custom.md)). Non-negotiable.
4. `jj describe -m "..." -m "..." -R .`: scratch working title. This first-time authoring is
   the one permitted describe. The commit is never published and never carries a trailer.

Nothing on a ladder is pushed. The close-out squash
(`jj squash --from "<base>..@-" --into @ -u -R .`) collapses it, and `vc-x1 push` then
publishes the single commit.

## Before any push

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval. Approval of a plan that includes a push
  is not push approval. "Commit and push" names the destination, not a waiver of the reviews.
  Only an explicit scoped delegation ("do all of X, don't check in") waives the stops, for that
  bounded task only. Delegation waives stops, never flow (records, validation, the bookmark
  discipline; see the protocol's [Policy](cycle-protocol.md#policy)), and destructive ops
  still pause.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are already written. Nothing follows the turn's final push (next checklist).

## After the final push: hard stop

Once the turn's final push or bot-repo squash-push is invoked, do no further work: no
verification, no summary, no next-step offers, no edits, until the user speaks. Put all closing
words *before* the invoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a visible token
after the tool returns. If so, emit a bare acknowledgment only (e.g. "landed"), never a summary
or more work. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's direction. A standing
delegation makes intermediate pushes just steps; the hard stop lands on the turn's *final*
push. See
[After push or squash-push](cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-squash-push-stop-and-wait).

## Close-out checklist

The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
[Close-out](cycle-protocol.md#close-out):

1. **Run the acceptance check** the opening stated, and record what it showed in the
   `## In Progress` block, whether or not it passed. A check that was never run is a failed
   close-out, and a check that failed is a finding, not a reason to quietly restate the banner.
2. **Finalize the six items in place**: sync the title if the scope shifted, replace the
   provisional solution statement with what was done, drop the ladder's `(current)` / `(done)`
   markers, add any design subsections, and write the closing rung's gotchas subsection
   (problem/solution form) if closing surfaced any.
3. **Move the block** into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, which is what creates the section.
   Four transforms, two of which fail silently: headings one level deeper, rung refs renumbered
   into the destination's namespace, repo-root-relative links gain `../`, forward-looking notes
   rewritten. See [Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections). Add the title-only
   `## Table of Contents` entry.
4. Write the `## Done` entry: the version, then a bold title line with its chores `[N]` ref,
   detail as sub-bullets (see [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form)). Replace the
   `## In Progress` block with `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
5. Full validation, mandatory.
6. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
7. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
   [in the protocol](cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe). Its step 4 is
   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
8. **Land the bookmark** on the user's go. Until this, nothing the cycle pushed is permanent.
   Once `main` contains the bookmark, delete it, locally and remotely. See
   [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land).
9. Backfill the chores as-built ladder refs (and any remaining legacy `Commits:` lines) for the
   commits landing just made permanent, which is the whole cycle rather than the previous push's
   share. Never record a SHA that is not on a permanent branch. The backfill edits ride the next
   push (a commit cannot record its own SHA).

## vc-x1 push behaviors to keep in mind

Three, independent of project language:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 assumes nothing about a repo's contents beyond
  `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`, and runs no build or tests. The medium's validation is the
  per-commit flow's job, run *before* invoking `vc-x1 push`. The one check that remains is
  `push-work` verifying the bookmark's remote refs are tracked, which is its own precondition.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume. Every stage no-ops when its
  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If a run fails, push stops and
  reports. Getting the repos back to a sensible state is the user's call, not something the
  tool infers.
- **ochid trailers** are injected by `vc-x1 push` itself, so don't hand-write them into the
  commit body or `--title`/`--body`.

content.content:
1	# Notes file conventions
2	
3	Conventions the bot follows when reading and writing notes files (`TODO.md`,
4	`notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md`, `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, `notes/done.md`). One
5	source of truth lives here, and [`notes/README.md`](../notes/README.md) points back. Read this
6	before editing a notes file.
7	
8	Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and
9	converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
10	Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).
11	
12	## File reads: read the slice you need
13	
14	Long notes files are appended to over time. Read only the slice your task needs. Grep or read
15	further on demand.
16	
17	- **`TODO.md`** (the routine acquaint read): the first ~60 lines covers intro + `## In
18	  Progress` + the top of the ranked `## Todo` (priorities, #1 highest). `Read` with
19	  `offset=0, limit=60`. `## Ideas` sits below `## Todo`. Read further only when chasing a
20	  lower-ranked entry, an Idea, a `[N]` ref, or auditing the whole list.
21	- **`notes/todo-backlog.md`**: the long-tail backlog (lower-priority entries below the ranked
22	  `## Todo`). Read only when picking up a backlog item, and grep to locate it first.
23	- **`notes/bugs.md`**: the bug list. Small, so read it whole when triaging a bug or chasing the
24	  `## Bugs` pointer in TODO.md.
25	- **`notes/done.md`** + **`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`**: historical / append-mostly. Scan
26	  headings first (`grep '^## ' notes/chores/chores-NN.md`), then read only the section you
27	  need.
28	
29	**Why:** the routine read should stay small. `TODO.md` grows every cycle, so the backlog and
30	bugs live in files under `notes/` rather than inline. The same "slice you need" rule applies
31	to historical files.
32	
33	## Notes references
34	
35	Reference *citations* are double-bracketed so the brackets render: `[[N]]`, or `[[2]],[[3]]`
36	for several (comma-separated, not `[2,3]` or `[[2]][[3]]`). The `[N]:` definitions in a file's
37	`# References` section and inline `[text](url)` / `[text](#anchor)` links stay
38	single-bracketed.
39	
40	## Reference numbering
41	
42	Every note file (`TODO.md`, `todo-backlog.md`, `bugs.md`, `chores-NN.md`, `done.md`) keeps a
43	file-local `# References` section at the bottom. Reference numbers are scoped to that file:
44	`[1]` in `chores-07.md` and `[1]` in `chores-01.md` are independent slots that may point at
45	completely different URLs. New chores files start their numbering at `[1]`.
46	
47	Treat `[N]` like a **footnote**: the number is a local slot, only meaningful within its file's
48	`# References`. So a `[N]` *citation* (bare `[N]`, or doubled `[[N]]`) never reuses another
49	file's number. To cite a target a sibling file references, pick your own next-local slot and
50	define it (the same target may carry a different number in each file). A `[N]` *inside a code
51	span* (`` `[72]` ``) is different: that's a quoted identifier, literal text naming a ref-key
52	(often from another file's namespace), data, not a citation, so it needs no definition here. To
53	point at a section of another file from prose, use an inline link with an anchor,
54	`[that section](../chores-07.md#...)`, not a bare number.
55	
56	A `chores-NN.md` `# References` entry is usually a `/notes/<file>.md#anchor` (or
57	`/ARCHITECTURE.md`) path, but may also be a **commit reference**,
58	`[N]: <commit-url-with-12-hex-SHA> "<full-40-hex-SHA>"`, cited by a rung of a section's
59	as-built ladder. See [Chores commit references](#chores-commit-references) for the why and the
60	exact shape.
61	
62	A file's `# References` can be **re-packed** to a contiguous `[1]..[N]` in
63	first-citation-appearance order: walk the file's prose in document order (`TODO.md`: `## Todo`
64	then `## Done`; `chores-NN.md`: top to bottom) and number refs as their first `[[N]]` citation
65	appears. This is a file-local rewrite, so only that file's `[[N]]` citations and `[N]:`
66	definitions move. Every target and sibling file is untouched. A `[[N]]` inside a `` ` `` code
67	span is a literal token, not a citation, and is left alone. Do it opportunistically (when the
68	namespace has drifted enough to annoy), not on a schedule: `TODO.md` fragments fastest (entries
69	land and get pruned every cycle) and is the usual candidate; `chores-NN.md` / `done.md` are
70	append-mostly and only need it after an unusual event (e.g. a bulk retrofit that allocated
71	slots out of document order).
72	
73	## Markdown anchor links
74	
75	GitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric characters in place, map remaining
76	spaces to hyphens 1-for-1. Do **not** collapse adjacent whitespace, so `a + b` -> `a--b`
77	(spaces on both sides of `+`), but `a: b` -> `a-b` (only trailing space on `:`). General
78	markdown reference: [markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub publishes no
79	official spec for auto-generated anchors. The de-facto reference implementation is
80	[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).
81	
82	## Todo format
83	
84	`TODO.md` is organized into `## In Progress`, `## Todo` (strict priority rank, #1 highest;
85	long-tail backlog in [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md)), `## Ideas`, `## Bugs`
86	(pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md)), and `## Done` sections. Each item is a short
87	description with reference links to more detail.
88	
89	`## Todo` and `## Bugs` entries carry explicit `1.` `2.` ... numbers in the source. For
90	`## Todo` the number is its **priority rank** (#1 highest, descending); for `## Bugs` it's just
91	an index. They're for grepping and at-a-glance "let's do #1", **not stable IDs**: reorder (to
92	reprioritize), insert, or delete freely, then `vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run` renumbers and
93	normalizes continuation-line indent, so any given number is positional. **To refer to a Todo
94	durably, name it by its title, a plain, greppable text mention.** Not its number (positional,
95	renumbered) and not a markdown link: a numbered list item has no anchor to link to.
96	
97	Numbering helps a human orient in a long list but makes links difficult and fragile, especially
98	an external reference pointing in, which can't be auto-fixed when the list renumbers. A robust
99	fix (a number-free anchor, or a number-tolerant dereference that matches the title slug and
100	wildcards the numeric prefix, since a GitHub slug like `5-foo` is encoded, not opaque, so the
101	title is recoverable) is a `validate-numbering` design question, out of scope here.
102	
103	`vc-x1 fix-todo` alone only previews, and `vc-x1 validate-todo` is the read-only check. The
104	`## Done` section keeps `-` bullets, since items aren't referenced by number once completed.
105	
106	Example shape:
107	
108	```
109	# Todo
110	1. Add new feature X [details](features.md#feature-x)
111	2. Fix bug Y [[1]]
112	
113	# Done
114	- **Fixed issue Z** [[2]],[[3]]
115	
116	[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
117	[2]: issues.md#issue-z
118	[3]: fixes.md#fix-z
119	```
120	
121	## Done entry form
122	
123	A `## Done` entry (in `TODO.md` and in `done.md`) is the close-out's **version**, then a **bold
124	title line** carrying its chores `[[N]]` ref, with any detail as sub-bullets:
125	
126	```
127	- 0.42.0 **feat: config loader** [[7]]
128	  - `--config` resolves per-profile pin pools
129	  - the parse rejects unknown keys rather than ignoring them
130	```
131	
132	- **Bold, and detail below rather than beside.** These entries are read by skimming a list for
133	  one of them, so the title has to be findable without reading the line it sits on. A title
134	  followed by a paragraph of summary is the wall-of-prose shape
135	  [Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) warns about, and it hides the one thing a skim is looking
136	  for. Bold matches the `## In Progress` block, whose title line is already bold.
137	- **The version leads and the title stays bold**, so the entry answers both questions a reader
138	  brings: `grep 0.42.0` finds what shipped in a version, and the eye still lands on titles when
139	  skimming. Putting the version *inside* the bold, or dropping the bold for a plain rung-shaped
140	  line, trades one of those for the other. See
141	  [Versions live in the version-of-record only](prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)
142	  for why a Done entry may carry a version at all when a ladder rung may not.
143	- **A one-liner is still fine** when the title says it all. The sub-bullets are for when it does
144	  not. What is not fine is the middle case, a title with sentences trailing off it.
145	- **Sub-bullets are conceptual, like chores bullets**: what shipped, not a file list, and never
146	  a copy of the chores intro. The `[[N]]` ref is what carries a reader to the full narrative.
147	- **Entries written before this convention keep their form** and gain a version when touched. A
148	  sweep would rewrite history's presentation for no reader's benefit.
149	
150	## Retiring Done entries
151	
152	`TODO.md`'s `## Done` section is a rolling buffer of recently shipped work, not a permanent
153	log. Move entries into `done.md` at these natural beats:
154	
155	- **Closing a ladder**: when the close-out commit ships, decide which prior entries are no
156	  longer needed for nearby context and migrate them. The entry form is the same in both files
157	  (see [Done entry form](#done-entry-form)), so a migration moves the bullet as it stands.
158	- **Opening a new ladder**: at the opening step, do the same sweep before bumping the
159	  version-of-record.
160	- **Resolving an agent-file experiment**: at the beat where it resolves, not at a ladder
161	  boundary. Adopted and rejected retire identically, since "we tried this and dropped it" is what
162	  history serves worst. The narrative goes in a `chores-NN.md` section and the dogfood entry is
163	  removed from wherever the project keeps its log, so that log carries in-flight entries only. See
164	  [Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files).
165	
166	Migration mechanics:
167	
168	- Move the bullet itself from `TODO.md > ## Done` to `done.md` (preserving the original ref
169	  number).
170	- Copy any references the moved entries cite into `done.md`'s `# References` section (those
171	  refs are file-local, so coexisting with `TODO.md`'s namespace is fine).
172	- Prune any references in `TODO.md > # References` no longer cited by anything in
173	  `## In Progress` / `## Todo` / `## Done`. This frees the numbers for future reuse.
174	
175	## Chores conventions
176	
177	### Headings and entries that record a commit
178	
179	A commit's title is reused verbatim across its records. See
180	[Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit) for the
181	rule. Beyond the chores `##` header, that same string is used for the matching
182	`TODO.md > ## Done` entry and any `[N]` reference to that section. **No title carries a
183	version.** The two records that carry one carry it beside the title, never inside it, and both
184	are records of a commit (the backfilled as-built rung and the `## Done` entry). See
185	[Versions live in the version-of-record only](prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only).
186	E.g. the chores header `## refactor: extract config loader` and the Done line
187	`- 0.42.0 **refactor: extract config loader** [[3]]`. The `## Done` entry uses the close-out
188	commit's title, and its shape is in [Done entry form](#done-entry-form).
189	
190	This does **not** apply to organizational headings (`## Todo`, `## In Progress`,
191	`# References`) or to design `###` subsections inside a chores section. Those are named for
192	whatever fits. Among the commit-recording ones, exact match is the strong default (nothing
193	absolute): a near-miss just makes it harder to line a record up with its commit.
194	
195	A commit-recording header is provisional while the work is in progress. The *last* edit before
196	`vc-x1 push` syncs it, and the `## Done` entry / `[N]` anchor for that commit, to the final
197	commit title. See [Markdown anchor links](#markdown-anchor-links) for the slug algorithm. The
198	pre-commit checklist catches a dangling `#anchor`, and a future `vc-x1 validate-repo` should
199	too (and should verify the recorded title matches the commit).
200	
201	Any pre-existing sections and `## Done` entries that predate this convention keep their
202	free-form text. The convention applies going forward.
203	
204	### Chores section content: no edit list; git is the record
205	
206	A chores section is: the as-built ladder (first content under the header, below), then
207	[Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) (intro + bullets) for what landed and why, and any `###`
208	design subsections. Bullets here are **conceptual** (design points, structural notes), never a
209	per-file edit list. Nothing in prose keeps one: the **diff** is the source of truth for what
210	changed mechanically (`git show --stat`, immutable, naturally scoped to the commit), the **commit
211	body** states the problem and the solution in broad terms, and the **chores section** is the
212	source of truth for the design thinking. Each of the three cross-links to the others; none
213	restates another.
214	
215	The section is **not built up here**: it is created at close-out by moving the cycle's
216	`## In Progress` block, which was its single home while the cycle ran. So a rung is appended, and
217	narrative written, in `TODO.md` as each step lands, and close-out moves the finished block rather
218	than assembling a second copy of it. Full when-in-the-cycle timing lives in cycle-protocol.md
219	[Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections). This note is the pointer, so the
220	two don't drift.
221	
222	**Why one home:** the alternative keeps a working ladder in `TODO.md` and an as-built ladder in
223	chores, so every rung is written twice and every backfill applied twice. Detail written twice
224	drifts, which is the same argument that keeps the edit list out of the commit body.
225	
226	When the intro starts wanting to explain a mechanism, hypothesis, or wrinkle, don't inflate it.
227	Promote that to its own `###` subsection inside the same `chores-NN.md`. If the wrinkle is a
228	live design concern (something that *should* change, not just be recorded), also add a
229	`TODO.md` item with a `[N]` ref pointing at that subsection (todo->chores is the normal ref
230	direction).
231	
232	**Why:** a chores edit list and the commit body were specified to be the same content in two
233	places, and detail written twice drifts. Git owns the mechanical record; the body owns the problem
234	and the solution; chores owns the narrative; the ladder's commit refs link them.
235	
236	### Chores commit references
237	
238	The first content under a chores section header is the **as-built ladder**: one rung per
239	commit the section records, in landing order, each rung carrying its own `[N]` citation slot.
240	The same form is used for every cycle, single- or multi-commit. A single-commit cycle is a
241	one-rung ladder whose one step is the close-out:
242	
243	```
244	## refactor: extract config loader
245	
246	- [[2]] 0.42.0-1 refactor: split loader from parser
247	- [[N]] refactor: extract config loader
248	
249	<intro paragraph...>
250	```
251	
252	- The rung form is `- [[N]] <title>` while the commit is unlanded, becoming
253	  `- [[2]] X.Y.Z[-n] <title>` at backfill, as the first rung above shows. No step number and no
254	  `(current)` / `(done)` marker, since as-built implies done (the in-flight markers live in
255	  `TODO.md > ## In Progress`). Landing order is the list order. See
256	  [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered).
257	- **The version arrives with the SHA, not before it.** It is the one version written into prose
258	  (see
259	  [Versions live in the version-of-record only](prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)),
260	  because here it records what a landed commit carried rather than naming a step, and together
261	  with the SHA it decodes an old `-V` banner. On an unlanded branch it is as rewritable as the
262	  SHA, so it waits for the same moment (Timing, below). The version is knowable earlier, from the
263	  manifest. Holding it back is deliberate, buying one timing rule and a record a rebase cannot
264	  falsify.
265	- Two headers in one chores file must not share a title, or their anchors collide and the
266	  duplicate silently resolves to the first. Within a file that is the whole uniqueness
267	  requirement. Titles may repeat across the repo's history.
268	- A rung is written with the literal `[[N]]` placeholder and backfilled in place with a real
269	  file-local slot once its commit's SHA is permanent (see Timing below).
270	- Rung citations use the file-local `[N]` reference machinery (see
271	  [Reference numbering](#reference-numbering)), **double-bracketed** so the brackets render.
272	  (`[[3]]` shows as a literal `[`, the `[3]` link, then a literal `]`; the inner `[3]`
273	  resolves against its `[3]:` definition, and CommonMark / GitHub / VS Code all do this.) The
274	  `# References` definition puts the **commit URL** as the destination, with the **full
275	  40-hex SHA** in the title slot:
276	
277	```
278	[3]: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/commit/<12-hex> "<40-hex>"
279	```
280	
281	- The 12-hex short SHA in the URL keeps it short, and GitHub / GitLab resolve a unique prefix to
282	  the canonical commit page (GitLab's path has a `/-/` before `commit/`).
283	- The full SHA in the title is host-agnostic and unambiguous: it survives a repo host change,
284	  `git show <40-hex>` works in any clone, and external tooling scraping the notes (a database,
285	  say) gets the canonical identifier.
286	
287	**Timing.** A commit's SHA isn't stable until it lands on a **permanent branch** (`main`, or a
288	long-lived release/patch branch), because a rebase or squash rewrites it on the way, and neither
289	is its version. A commit can't record its own SHA, so the fill lands one push later: every rung
290	opens with the literal `[[N]]` placeholder and no version, and each push backfills the rungs of
291	the commits the previous push made permanent. On a topic branch a section waits until the branch
292	lands. The commit itself is the record, and `git log --grep "<title>"` finds it. See
293	cycle-protocol [Commits backfill](cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill).
294	
295	Sections that predate this convention keep their `Commits:` lines. The ladder form applies
296	going forward.
297	
298	### Chores file Table of Contents
299	
300	Each `chores-NN.md` carries a `## Table of Contents` section between the file intro and the
301	first commit-recording section: one `- [<title>](#<anchor>)` entry per commit-recording `##`
302	section, in file order.
303	
304	- Entries are title-only, with no version and no `[N]` refs, so the TOC never needs backfill:
305	  the TOC navigates, the section's as-built ladder records.
306	- The entry is appended by the close-out move that creates the section, and the entry text
307	  participates in the same last-edit title sync as the section header and the `## Done` entry.
308	- Design `###` subsections stay out of the TOC.
309	- Files predating the convention gain a TOC opportunistically, not on a schedule.

# Notes file conventions

Conventions the bot follows when reading and writing notes files (`TODO.md`,
`notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md`, `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, `notes/done.md`). One
source of truth lives here, and [`notes/README.md`](../notes/README.md) points back. Read this
before editing a notes file.

Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and
converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## File reads: read the slice you need

Long notes files are appended to over time. Read only the slice your task needs. Grep or read
further on demand.

- **`TODO.md`** (the routine acquaint read): the first ~60 lines covers intro + `## In
  Progress` + the top of the ranked `## Todo` (priorities, #1 highest). `Read` with
  `offset=0, limit=60`. `## Ideas` sits below `## Todo`. Read further only when chasing a
  lower-ranked entry, an Idea, a `[N]` ref, or auditing the whole list.
- **`notes/todo-backlog.md`**: the long-tail backlog (lower-priority entries below the ranked
  `## Todo`). Read only when picking up a backlog item, and grep to locate it first.
- **`notes/bugs.md`**: the bug list. Small, so read it whole when triaging a bug or chasing the
  `## Bugs` pointer in TODO.md.
- **`notes/done.md`** + **`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`**: historical / append-mostly. Scan
  headings first (`grep '^## ' notes/chores/chores-NN.md`), then read only the section you
  need.

**Why:** the routine read should stay small. `TODO.md` grows every cycle, so the backlog and
bugs live in files under `notes/` rather than inline. The same "slice you need" rule applies
to historical files.

## Notes references

Reference *citations* are double-bracketed so the brackets render: `[[N]]`, or `[[2]],[[3]]`
for several (comma-separated, not `[2,3]` or `[[2]][[3]]`). The `[N]:` definitions in a file's
`# References` section and inline `[text](url)` / `[text](#anchor)` links stay
single-bracketed.

## Reference numbering

Every note file (`TODO.md`, `todo-backlog.md`, `bugs.md`, `chores-NN.md`, `done.md`) keeps a
file-local `# References` section at the bottom. Reference numbers are scoped to that file:
`[1]` in `chores-07.md` and `[1]` in `chores-01.md` are independent slots that may point at
completely different URLs. New chores files start their numbering at `[1]`.

Treat `[N]` like a **footnote**: the number is a local slot, only meaningful within its file's
`# References`. So a `[N]` *citation* (bare `[N]`, or doubled `[[N]]`) never reuses another
file's number. To cite a target a sibling file references, pick your own next-local slot and
define it (the same target may carry a different number in each file). A `[N]` *inside a code
span* (`` `[72]` ``) is different: that's a quoted identifier, literal text naming a ref-key
(often from another file's namespace), data, not a citation, so it needs no definition here. To
point at a section of another file from prose, use an inline link with an anchor,
`[that section](../chores-07.md#...)`, not a bare number.

A `chores-NN.md` `# References` entry is usually a `/notes/<file>.md#anchor` (or
`/ARCHITECTURE.md`) path, but may also be a **commit reference**,
`[N]: <commit-url-with-12-hex-SHA> "<full-40-hex-SHA>"`, cited by a rung of a section's
as-built ladder. See [Chores commit references](#chores-commit-references) for the why and the
exact shape.

A file's `# References` can be **re-packed** to a contiguous `[1]..[N]` in
first-citation-appearance order: walk the file's prose in document order (`TODO.md`: `## Todo`
then `## Done`; `chores-NN.md`: top to bottom) and number refs as their first `[[N]]` citation
appears. This is a file-local rewrite, so only that file's `[[N]]` citations and `[N]:`
definitions move. Every target and sibling file is untouched. A `[[N]]` inside a `` ` `` code
span is a literal token, not a citation, and is left alone. Do it opportunistically (when the
namespace has drifted enough to annoy), not on a schedule: `TODO.md` fragments fastest (entries
land and get pruned every cycle) and is the usual candidate; `chores-NN.md` / `done.md` are
append-mostly and only need it after an unusual event (e.g. a bulk retrofit that allocated
slots out of document order).

## Markdown anchor links

GitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric characters in place, map remaining
spaces to hyphens 1-for-1. Do **not** collapse adjacent whitespace, so `a + b` -> `a--b`
(spaces on both sides of `+`), but `a: b` -> `a-b` (only trailing space on `:`). General
markdown reference: [markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub publishes no
official spec for auto-generated anchors. The de-facto reference implementation is
[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).

## Todo format

`TODO.md` is organized into `## In Progress`, `## Todo` (strict priority rank, #1 highest;
long-tail backlog in [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md)), `## Ideas`, `## Bugs`
(pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md)), and `## Done` sections. Each item is a short
description with reference links to more detail.

`## Todo` and `## Bugs` entries carry explicit `1.` `2.` ... numbers in the source. For
`## Todo` the number is its **priority rank** (#1 highest, descending); for `## Bugs` it's just
an index. They're for grepping and at-a-glance "let's do #1", **not stable IDs**: reorder (to
reprioritize), insert, or delete freely, then `vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run` renumbers and
normalizes continuation-line indent, so any given number is positional. **To refer to a Todo
durably, name it by its title, a plain, greppable text mention.** Not its number (positional,
renumbered) and not a markdown link: a numbered list item has no anchor to link to.

Numbering helps a human orient in a long list but makes links difficult and fragile, especially
an external reference pointing in, which can't be auto-fixed when the list renumbers. A robust
fix (a number-free anchor, or a number-tolerant dereference that matches the title slug and
wildcards the numeric prefix, since a GitHub slug like `5-foo` is encoded, not opaque, so the
title is recoverable) is a `validate-numbering` design question, out of scope here.

`vc-x1 fix-todo` alone only previews, and `vc-x1 validate-todo` is the read-only check. The
`## Done` section keeps `-` bullets, since items aren't referenced by number once completed.

Example shape:

```
# Todo
1. Add new feature X [details](features.md#feature-x)
2. Fix bug Y [[1]]

# Done
- **Fixed issue Z** [[2]],[[3]]

[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
[2]: issues.md#issue-z
[3]: fixes.md#fix-z
```

## Done entry form

A `## Done` entry (in `TODO.md` and in `done.md`) is the close-out's **version**, then a **bold
title line** carrying its chores `[[N]]` ref, with any detail as sub-bullets:

```
- 0.42.0 **feat: config loader** [[7]]
  - `--config` resolves per-profile pin pools
  - the parse rejects unknown keys rather than ignoring them
```

- **Bold, and detail below rather than beside.** These entries are read by skimming a list for
  one of them, so the title has to be findable without reading the line it sits on. A title
  followed by a paragraph of summary is the wall-of-prose shape
  [Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) warns about, and it hides the one thing a skim is looking
  for. Bold matches the `## In Progress` block, whose title line is already bold.
- **The version leads and the title stays bold**, so the entry answers both questions a reader
  brings: `grep 0.42.0` finds what shipped in a version, and the eye still lands on titles when
  skimming. Putting the version *inside* the bold, or dropping the bold for a plain rung-shaped
  line, trades one of those for the other. See
  [Versions live in the version-of-record only](prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)
  for why a Done entry may carry a version at all when a ladder rung may not.
- **A one-liner is still fine** when the title says it all. The sub-bullets are for when it does
  not. What is not fine is the middle case, a title with sentences trailing off it.
- **Sub-bullets are conceptual, like chores bullets**: what shipped, not a file list, and never
  a copy of the chores intro. The `[[N]]` ref is what carries a reader to the full narrative.
- **Entries written before this convention keep their form** and gain a version when touched. A
  sweep would rewrite history's presentation for no reader's benefit.

## Retiring Done entries

`TODO.md`'s `## Done` section is a rolling buffer of recently shipped work, not a permanent
log. Move entries into `done.md` at these natural beats:

- **Closing a ladder**: when the close-out commit ships, decide which prior entries are no
  longer needed for nearby context and migrate them. The entry form is the same in both files
  (see [Done entry form](#done-entry-form)), so a migration moves the bullet as it stands.
- **Opening a new ladder**: at the opening step, do the same sweep before bumping the
  version-of-record.
- **Resolving an agent-file experiment**: at the beat where it resolves, not at a ladder
  boundary. Adopted and rejected retire identically, since "we tried this and dropped it" is what
  history serves worst. The narrative goes in a `chores-NN.md` section and the dogfood entry is
  removed from wherever the project keeps its log, so that log carries in-flight entries only. See
  [Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files).

Migration mechanics:

- Move the bullet itself from `TODO.md > ## Done` to `done.md` (preserving the original ref
  number).
- Copy any references the moved entries cite into `done.md`'s `# References` section (those
  refs are file-local, so coexisting with `TODO.md`'s namespace is fine).
- Prune any references in `TODO.md > # References` no longer cited by anything in
  `## In Progress` / `## Todo` / `## Done`. This frees the numbers for future reuse.

## Chores conventions

### Headings and entries that record a commit

A commit's title is reused verbatim across its records. See
[Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit) for the
rule. Beyond the chores `##` header, that same string is used for the matching
`TODO.md > ## Done` entry and any `[N]` reference to that section. **No title carries a
version.** The two records that carry one carry it beside the title, never inside it, and both
are records of a commit (the backfilled as-built rung and the `## Done` entry). See
[Versions live in the version-of-record only](prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only).
E.g. the chores header `## refactor: extract config loader` and the Done line
`- 0.42.0 **refactor: extract config loader** [[3]]`. The `## Done` entry uses the close-out
commit's title, and its shape is in [Done entry form](#done-entry-form).

This does **not** apply to organizational headings (`## Todo`, `## In Progress`,
`# References`) or to design `###` subsections inside a chores section. Those are named for
whatever fits. Among the commit-recording ones, exact match is the strong default (nothing
absolute): a near-miss just makes it harder to line a record up with its commit.

A commit-recording header is provisional while the work is in progress. The *last* edit before
`vc-x1 push` syncs it, and the `## Done` entry / `[N]` anchor for that commit, to the final
commit title. See [Markdown anchor links](#markdown-anchor-links) for the slug algorithm. The
pre-commit checklist catches a dangling `#anchor`, and a future `vc-x1 validate-repo` should
too (and should verify the recorded title matches the commit).

Any pre-existing sections and `## Done` entries that predate this convention keep their
free-form text. The convention applies going forward.

### Chores section content: no edit list; git is the record

A chores section is: the as-built ladder (first content under the header, below), then
[Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) (intro + bullets) for what landed and why, and any `###`
design subsections. Bullets here are **conceptual** (design points, structural notes), never a
per-file edit list. Nothing in prose keeps one: the **diff** is the source of truth for what
changed mechanically (`git show --stat`, immutable, naturally scoped to the commit), the **commit
body** states the problem and the solution in broad terms, and the **chores section** is the
source of truth for the design thinking. Each of the three cross-links to the others; none
restates another.

The section is **not built up here**: it is created at close-out by moving the cycle's
`## In Progress` block, which was its single home while the cycle ran. So a rung is appended, and
narrative written, in `TODO.md` as each step lands, and close-out moves the finished block rather
than assembling a second copy of it. Full when-in-the-cycle timing lives in cycle-protocol.md
[Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections). This note is the pointer, so the
two don't drift.

**Why one home:** the alternative keeps a working ladder in `TODO.md` and an as-built ladder in
chores, so every rung is written twice and every backfill applied twice. Detail written twice
drifts, which is the same argument that keeps the edit list out of the commit body.

When the intro starts wanting to explain a mechanism, hypothesis, or wrinkle, don't inflate it.
Promote that to its own `###` subsection inside the same `chores-NN.md`. If the wrinkle is a
live design concern (something that *should* change, not just be recorded), also add a
`TODO.md` item with a `[N]` ref pointing at that subsection (todo->chores is the normal ref
direction).

**Why:** a chores edit list and the commit body were specified to be the same content in two
places, and detail written twice drifts. Git owns the mechanical record; the body owns the problem
and the solution; chores owns the narrative; the ladder's commit refs link them.

### Chores commit references

The first content under a chores section header is the **as-built ladder**: one rung per
commit the section records, in landing order, each rung carrying its own `[N]` citation slot.
The same form is used for every cycle, single- or multi-commit. A single-commit cycle is a
one-rung ladder whose one step is the close-out:

```
## refactor: extract config loader

- [[2]] 0.42.0-1 refactor: split loader from parser
- [[N]] refactor: extract config loader

<intro paragraph...>
```

- The rung form is `- [[N]] <title>` while the commit is unlanded, becoming
  `- [[2]] X.Y.Z[-n] <title>` at backfill, as the first rung above shows. No step number and no
  `(current)` / `(done)` marker, since as-built implies done (the in-flight markers live in
  `TODO.md > ## In Progress`). Landing order is the list order. See
  [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered).
- **The version arrives with the SHA, not before it.** It is the one version written into prose
  (see
  [Versions live in the version-of-record only](prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)),
  because here it records what a landed commit carried rather than naming a step, and together
  with the SHA it decodes an old `-V` banner. On an unlanded branch it is as rewritable as the
  SHA, so it waits for the same moment (Timing, below). The version is knowable earlier, from the
  manifest. Holding it back is deliberate, buying one timing rule and a record a rebase cannot
  falsify.
- Two headers in one chores file must not share a title, or their anchors collide and the
  duplicate silently resolves to the first. Within a file that is the whole uniqueness
  requirement. Titles may repeat across the repo's history.
- A rung is written with the literal `[[N]]` placeholder and backfilled in place with a real
  file-local slot once its commit's SHA is permanent (see Timing below).
- Rung citations use the file-local `[N]` reference machinery (see
  [Reference numbering](#reference-numbering)), **double-bracketed** so the brackets render.
  (`[[3]]` shows as a literal `[`, the `[3]` link, then a literal `]`; the inner `[3]`
  resolves against its `[3]:` definition, and CommonMark / GitHub / VS Code all do this.) The
  `# References` definition puts the **commit URL** as the destination, with the **full
  40-hex SHA** in the title slot:

```
[3]: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/commit/<12-hex> "<40-hex>"
```

- The 12-hex short SHA in the URL keeps it short, and GitHub / GitLab resolve a unique prefix to
  the canonical commit page (GitLab's path has a `/-/` before `commit/`).
- The full SHA in the title is host-agnostic and unambiguous: it survives a repo host change,
  `git show <40-hex>` works in any clone, and external tooling scraping the notes (a database,
  say) gets the canonical identifier.

**Timing.** A commit's SHA isn't stable until it lands on a **permanent branch** (`main`, or a
long-lived release/patch branch), because a rebase or squash rewrites it on the way, and neither
is its version. A commit can't record its own SHA, so the fill lands one push later: every rung
opens with the literal `[[N]]` placeholder and no version, and each push backfills the rungs of
the commits the previous push made permanent. On a topic branch a section waits until the branch
lands. The commit itself is the record, and `git log --grep "<title>"` finds it. See
cycle-protocol [Commits backfill](cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill).

Sections that predate this convention keep their `Commits:` lines. The ladder form applies
going forward.

### Chores file Table of Contents

Each `chores-NN.md` carries a `## Table of Contents` section between the file intro and the
first commit-recording section: one `- [<title>](#<anchor>)` entry per commit-recording `##`
section, in file order.

- Entries are title-only, with no version and no `[N]` refs, so the TOC never needs backfill:
  the TOC navigates, the section's as-built ladder records.
- The entry is appended by the close-out move that creates the section, and the entry text
  participates in the same last-edit title sync as the section header and the `## Done` entry.
- Design `###` subsections stay out of the TOC.
- Files predating the convention gain a TOC opportunistically, not on a schedule.

# Todo

This file contains near term tasks with a short description
and reference links to more details.

Intro paragraphs in `## Todo` and `## Bugs` should begin every
line with 1 leading space so they don't match the `^\d+\. `
pattern that locates numbered entries; 2 or 3 spaces also work.

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. At Preparation
the picked-up `## Todo` item **moves** here (never copied, one home per text) and becomes six
provisional items, all required, all revised as steps land. At close-out the whole block moves
into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and becomes that cycle's `##` section. It is never written in
two places. Shape:

```
### <type>: <title>

#### Problem
<what is wrong, a sentence or two>

#### Solution
<what will be done about it, broad; provisional until the close-out>

#### Acceptance check
<the measure of "are you finished?">

#### Ladder
- <title> opening (done)
- <title> (current)
- <title>
- <close-out title>

#### Deliberation
<how the five above were decided; `_None._` if there was nothing to deliberate>
```

A multi-cycle program adds one level: the program is the `###`, its current cycle the `####`,
and the six items sit one level below that (headings give the current work durable anchors,
which numbered Todo entries can't). Full rules in
[cycle-protocol.md](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#preparation); the move's four transforms are
in [Chores sections](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

_The program block below predates the six-item convention and is grandfathered. Its versioned
rungs convert when touched._

### Refactor: typed jj facade -> jj-lib in-process; end subprocess spawning

Version-control operations were ~30 hand-rolled `run("jj", ...)`
spawns plus every mutation, with per-module private wrappers
and raw-git vestiges in init: stderr parsing instead of typed
errors, and jj's single-attempt index-lock acquisition (the
push `bookmark-set` lock race in [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md))
can't be retried where it fails. A multi-ladder program; the
staged plan, design detail, and the eight absorbed former
Todos live in
[refactor-20260716.md](notes/refactor-20260716.md).

[docs: adopt the merged agent-file set](#docs-adopt-the-merged-agent-file-set) above, its six
items were written here directly at close-out, the opening and close-out collapsing into the
one commit.

wink proposed forbidding semicolons in all prose, agent-files and code documentation included,
to shrink and simplify the rules. Review found the footprint already small (one prose.md
section plus three passing mentions) and every prose semicolon in AGENTS.md to be the
antithesis-between-equals form the rule protects. What stood after the argument was a narrower
preference: the family's top-level file should read without any.

The three joins reword with no information change, and nothing else moves:

- the hard-rule contrast ("costs seconds / costs much more") takes ", while"

  commas that a ", and" join would blur into

  only AGENTS.md wording

`grep -n ';' AGENTS.md` returns only lines whose semicolons sit inside backtick code spans,
and the reworded sentences carry the same claims as before. Ran at close-out: pass, the three
remaining hits being the shell specimens under "One command per shell invocation" and "Never
mask a command's exit status".

### Deliberation

- the outright ban was argued down on four points: the current rule already names and bans the
  lazy joins, the enforcement rationale that makes the typeable-punctuation rule absolute
  (untypeable, ungreppable) does not transfer to an ASCII character, a ban still needs the
  syntax-versus-prose and authored-versus-transcribed judgments so it cannot become a byte
  scan, and the whole footprint at stake is about fifteen lines of one file

  diff/history pair became two sentences instead of taking the ", and" the other pair took

  quotation of this file's older wording rather than a live sentence, acceptable for a
  specimen and left to converge at the template

The line-width numbers were restated at eight sites across four pinned files, so changing one
meant hunting the rest. And the commit-body width (72, git's older log-indent convention) was
not the Linux kernel patch standard (75) wink understood the project to have adopted.

becomes a pointer to it:

- the subsection holds all four numbers (prose <=100, source <=100, titles <=50, bodies <=75)

  drift. This cycle exists because the copies were already one drift into disagreement with

## fix: validate-desc from the bot side

- [[N]] fix: validate-desc from the bot side

A single-commit cycle, its six items written here directly at close-out like the sections
above. Reported by wink 2026-08-14: `validate-desc` run from inside `.claude` died with
"workspace incoherent ... `repos.work` resolves to <work repo>, not to the workspace root
itself". The cycle ran on the `fix-validate-desc` bookmark off `main` while the
docs-freshen-vc-config-and-config-subcmd cycle was still in flight on its own bookmark; the
fix was first written and verified against that branch's tip, then ported here (the patch
applied to `main` unchanged).

### Problem

`validate-desc` and `fix-desc` resolved "the other repo" by handing `params.repo` (default
`.`) to `bot_repo_path`, whose contract says its argument is the workspace root. Run from the
work repo that is accidentally true; run from the bot repo it is not, and the coherence
preflight's self-identification check (correctly) rejected the bot dir posing as the root. The
check was right, the caller was lying to it: neither command was ever taught sides.

### Solution

A side-aware resolver, used by both commands in place of the direct `bot_repo_path` call:

- `other_repo_path(repo)` finds the workspace root *from* the given repo path
  (`find_workspace_root_from`, which already follows a bot-side config's `work` entry up to
  the real root), runs the existing coherence preflight against that true root, and returns
  the far side: the bot repo when `repo` sits on the work side, the work repo when `repo`
  sits in the bot repo
- the bot side is tested first with `starts_with`, because the bot dir nests inside the work
  repo, so "under the root" alone cannot separate the sides
- `Ok(None)` still means a POR / single-repo workspace, both commands' no-op case, and legacy
  configs still reject via the preflight
- `bot_repo_path` itself is unchanged apart from its doc comment; its other callers all pass
  a real `find_workspace_root()` result

### Acceptance check

From a dual fixture's bot dir, `validate-desc` (and by the same code path `fix-desc`)
resolves the other repo as the work side and validates commits cleanly; from the work side
behavior is unchanged; a POR still no-ops; the full suite passes. Ran at close-out: pass
(three new `other_repo_path` unit tests, the from-bot-side one being the regression case,
plus a live toml-carrier fixture run both directions and `cargo fmt` / clippy `-D warnings` /
`cargo test` / install all green).

### Deliberation

- fix off `main` rather than a rung of the in-flight docs cycle (wink, 2026-08-14): the bug
  predates that branch, and below it the branch's later rename rung sweeps the fix's
  identifiers along as ordinary development instead of forcing repeated conflict resolution
  above it
- the freed triple: `0.78.8` was the docs branch's claimed version; wink chose to give it to
  this fix, the branch renumbering forward-only to its next triple at rebase time (recorded
  in that cycle's records at the renumber beat)
- a new helper over teaching `bot_repo_path` to walk: its contract (argument *is* the root)
  is what its other callers rely on, so the side-awareness lives in a wrapper and the
  contract stays

# References

[1]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/commit/a8b43a18999e "a8b43a18999ece30e7b807650ba45eb9b236ebdc"

475	##### fix: bot-session reads the md carrier
476	
477	- intent: `bot_session::workspace_bot_session` reads `root.join(".vc-config.toml")` through
478	  `toml_simple::toml_load`, so with both sides on the md carrier the file does not exist, the
479	  function returns all-`None`, and the workspace layer of `[bot-session]` settings is silently
480	  gone. A live regression from the handler rung's carrier switch
481	  - that rung's claim that every reader goes through `config_md::load` was scoped to the
482	    topology readers; this scalar reader was never converted and no test covered it
483	  - fix: route it through `config_md::load`, so a both-carriers or bad-fence config errors
484	    here as it does everywhere else rather than degrading to the user config in silence
485	  - a test setting a `[bot-session]` key in a `.vc-config.md` fixture and reading it back,
486	    since the silence is what made this invisible
487	- landed: the read splits into `bot_session_at(root)` and a cwd-anchored wrapper, matching
488	  `find_workspace_root_from`'s shape, and the core goes through `config_md::load`. Three
489	  tests: a `[bot-session]` block in a `.vc-config.md` arrives, a config without one is a plain
490	  miss, and both carriers on one side errors
491	  - **correction to the intent above**: the regression was latent, not live. `main`'s
492	    `.vc-config.toml` shipped the `[bot-session]` block with every key commented out, so no

##### fix: bot-session reads the md carrier

- intent: `bot_session::workspace_bot_session` reads `root.join(".vc-config.toml")` through
  `toml_simple::toml_load`, so with both sides on the md carrier the file does not exist, the
  function returns all-`None`, and the workspace layer of `[bot-session]` settings is silently
  gone. A live regression from the handler rung's carrier switch
  - that rung's claim that every reader goes through `config_md::load` was scoped to the
    topology readers; this scalar reader was never converted and no test covered it
  - fix: route it through `config_md::load`, so a both-carriers or bad-fence config errors
    here as it does everywhere else rather than degrading to the user config in silence
  - a test setting a `[bot-session]` key in a `.vc-config.md` fixture and reading it back,
    since the silence is what made this invisible
- landed: the read splits into `bot_session_at(root)` and a cwd-anchored wrapper, matching
  `find_workspace_root_from`'s shape, and the core goes through `config_md::load`. Three
  tests: a `[bot-session]` block in a `.vc-config.md` arrives, a config without one is a plain
  miss, and both carriers on one side errors
  - **correction to the intent above**: the regression was latent, not live. `main`'s
    `.vc-config.toml` shipped the `[bot-session]` block with every key commented out, so no
    workspace value was actually being dropped. The dropping capability was real and a set key
    would have vanished, which is what the fix removes
  - so the ordering held for a better reason than the one given: [the regenerate rung][41]
    re-emits these blocks, and a reader who uncommented one after that would have hit silence

##### docs: config-surface records, bold backlog titles

- intent: triaging iiac-perf's `.vc-config.md` review produced verdicts with nowhere to live.
  A mailbox reply's "Done when" cannot itself be the record, since handling the message deletes
  it, so every verdict needed a home before the reply could honestly claim one
- landed: the config-surface half is one bug and three entries. bugs.md gains
  **`config --validate` reports "I gave up" as a finding** (#9), where reading the code found
  `validate` breaking its own documented contract. `## Todo` gains
  **Tiered exit status for `config --validate`** (#5) and
  **`config --toml`: print the TOML a markdown carrier yields** (#6), both ranked on wink's
  call; todo-backlog keeps **Config provenance names the schema, not just the binary** (#55).
  The `toml`-tag escape is documented at [the regenerate rung][41] rather than spot-fixed
  - the notes-file half was not planned and came from the work itself: ranking two entries
    renumbered 17 and invalidated citations written minutes earlier, one already drafted into
    another member's mailbox. That produced
    **Cite a Todo or backlog entry by its bold title, not its number** (#56), its precondition
    swept here (32 backlog entries gained bold titles, none duplicated), and
    **What carries a Todo entry: numbered list, heading, or a tracker outside the repo?** (#57)
    for the structural question underneath, wink's, where the crux is that issues and a
    database both move records out of the repo and so change doctrine rather than format
  - **freeze lifted for this one rung** (wink, 2026-08-12), the same exception and the same
